note: Version-independent hook intent. Anchors are PATTERNS with <name:kind> captures; payloads reference those captures so registers and renamed types resolve automatically. Authored by diffing the same seven hooks as resolved against Instagram 430 and 439. JSON rather than YAML to stay dependency-free and match the repo's strict-decoding style.

probe.note: Not toggleable, so no two-directional delta exists. Executing at startup without a fatal IS the proof: an unresolved reference would throw here before any UI.

hooks.intent: Fail outgoing API requests whose URI path is blocked, as a normal request failure

hosts.note: stable named class; only its parameter types were renamed 430->439

constraints: MUST sit inside a try range whose .catch handles Ljava/io/IOException; outside it, a blocked request becomes a crash
the :try_start_0 anchor line is load-bearing: the iget alone is not unique

probe.note: HOOK-scoped, not feature-scoped. One code site enforces all five rules and the exception carries no path, so the count is 'this mechanism fired', not 'the feed rule fired'. The off-side therefore needs ALL five toggles off: measured on 439, all-on gives 10 canonical and all-off gives 0, while turning off only Disable feed leaves 2 - genuine live blocks of the other four rules, confirmed by a throwIfBlocked <- TigonServiceLayer.startRequest stack. A per-feature probe would need a path-scoped signal, which this log line does not provide.

intent_constraints: a blocked request must fail the way a normal network failure fails, not crash the app

hooks.intent: Blank the Reels discover request path when Reels are disabled

hosts.note: the class moved LX/05t2->LX/04tC; the literal did not. This literal alone appears in 5 classes on 430 and 5 on 439, and the anchor matches cleanly in 3 of them - analytics maps and prefetch allowlists load the same string. Only the class that builds the outgoing request path carries all three Reels endpoints, which is exactly one class on each version.

constraints: the result must be written back to the SAME register the literal was loaded into; the repeated <r> capture enforces this
idempotence marker is a COMMENT, never a no-op label: baksmali deletes unreferenced labels

probe.note: Block-counting CANNOT measure this hook. replaceReelsEndpoint blanks the endpoint upstream of throwIfBlocked, so the path never matches the blocklist and no IOException is produced. Zero blocks in both directions is expected, not a pass. Measured on 439: 3 canonical failures with Reels enabled and 0 with it disabled, so the Reels block is verified as a GROUP. This hook is NOT individually verified: all three replacements emit the identical line 'onClipsItemsRequestFailed [fetch]: status 404' with no endpoint qualifier, and one toggle governs all three, so if one replacement were inert the other two would still produce the signal. That is the 340 minshop failure mode - a substitution that never matched, hidden inside a group that worked. Attribution needs a surface that exercises only this endpoint. NEVER EXECUTED on 439 and probably legacy. Unlike homecoming it lives in a different method (A08), whose context carries the literal `android_purge_26_q2_ClipsDiscoverApiUtil_createRequestTask` - Instagram has flagged that path for removal in 2026 Q2. Not proven unreachable; revisit when that purge lands. DECISION 2026-08-01 (human): KEEP. The hook costs one instruction and blocking a path Instagram is retiring is harmless, whereas dropping it would leave a gap if the purge slips or the path outlives its marker. REVISIT when an Instagram release actually removes ClipsDiscoverApiUtil: at that point the by_literal host search stops finding a class carrying all three Reels literals, the co_literals intersection empties, and the Resolve stage escalates on its own rather than silently dropping the hook - so this decision fails loudly rather than rotting.

intent_constraints: when the feature is enabled the app must behave exactly as stock

hooks.intent: Open the DFInsta settings dialog by long-pressing Options on the user's own profile (ProfileActionBar variant)

hosts.note: MEASURED, not proposed by an agent. The host is the one class in the decode whose body matches this hook's own five-line anchor. Verified on two versions: 439 -> LX/0DnT; (1 of 181,421 classes) and 430 -> LX/077K; (1 of 179,190), each the host the hand-done port established. Cross-checked against a full unprefiltered match over every class in both decodes: same single class each time, so the byte-level prefilter derived from the anchor ('}, Landroid/view/View;->setLayoutParams(Landroid/view/ViewGroup$LayoutParams;)V', 986 survivors on 439 and 930 on 430) is an accelerator and not part of the answer. WHY THIS IS ENOUGH EVIDENCE TO DROP proposer_agreement AND adversarial_verified: those exist because an agent's descriptor is an assertion nothing else checks, and a 430 descriptor still names a live class in 439. Here nothing is carried between versions - the anchor is re-matched against the target decode every port, and it is the SAME text the patch is spliced into, so a version where it stops identifying the host is a version where it stops identifying the site, and the hook escalates rather than resolving somewhere wrong. Two independent uniqueness claims still both have to hold: exactly one class in the decode matches (or the search reports AMBIGUOUS and names them), and the anchor matches exactly once inside it (expected_anchor_count, which is what grew this anchor from three lines to five). WHAT IS GENUINELY LOST: nobody re-reads the class to ask whether it is the right one for the right reason. The 439 adversarial verifier's finding about the OTHER settings variant - that its patch site may be unreachable at runtime - is exactly the kind of thing this cannot see, and the ui_dialog probe cannot separate the two variants either. So this makes host discovery mechanical; it does not make the hook self-verifying.

constraints: the last TWO anchor lines are the discriminator, not decoration. The three-line 'build a listener, attach it' idiom is generic: it matches 3 times in the 439 host and 2 times in the 430 host, and the resolver refused both as ambiguous. Only the site that builds the Options ImageView is followed by setLayoutParams on the SAME register the listener was attached to AND then returns that register. The other-user follow button (new-instance ...FadeInFollowButton) calls the button's own setup method instead and must be excluded — attaching there would put the DFInsta dialog on a stranger's Follow button. The third 439 site does call setLayoutParams on <view> but then falls through to a goto rather than returning, so requiring `return-object <view>` is what excludes it.

mode is `replace` BECAUSE the anchor now ends at `return-object`. With `insert_after` the payload would land after a return and be unreachable — statically perfect, runtime-inert, which is the failure this project has shipped more often than any other. The payload therefore re-emits the anchor verbatim and splices the DFInsta lines in BEFORE the return, keeping setLayoutParams and the return as the last two instructions.

must be restricted to the user's OWN profile; other users' Options must stay non-long-clickable. This method builds the icon for EVERY action-bar model type — every branch merges on the label just above the anchor — so an unguarded attach makes a stranger's controls long-clickable. The shipped patch guards with `instance-of <r>, <model>, LX/077N;` (430) / `LX/0Dxw;` (439) plus `if-eqz` around the DFInsta lines only, never around the stock lines.

the guard's two values are the ONLY thing the anchor cannot reach, and the wider anchor does not change that: the register holding the action model is the 4th init argument on 430 (p3, capture <d>) and the 2nd on 439 (p4, capture <b>), so no one capture NAME holds it across versions; and the self-profile type moved LX/077N -> LX/0Dxw and is named on no line adjacent to this site, so no anchor extension can capture it. What the wider anchor does buy is that the SITE is mechanical: host in, one anchor out, on both 430 and 439.

<model> and <selfprofile> are therefore filled from supplied_captures, NOT from requires_proposal. requires_proposal must not be re-added: Resolve tests it against `sited` candidates and returns NEEDS_AGENT before the supply pass ever runs, so the flag and the supply group cannot both be set — the flag wins and the supplier is dead code. The safety the flag provided is not lost, it moved: a supply group that cannot be filled escalates to NEEDS_AGENT with the capture names, and merge_supplied kind-checks every supplied value at the render boundary, so an unfillable guard still refuses to render rather than emitting an unguarded attach.
the listener register is dead after the stock helper call consumes it, which is why it is safe to reuse

probe.note: Not toggleable. The proof is that the dialog opens at all; before the 430 re-map this hook applied cleanly and was completely inert. Measured on 439: the dialog opens. NOT individually attributable - the other settings variant declares the same signal on the same surface, and Instagram picks between the two action-bar implementations at runtime, so exactly one is live and the observation cannot say which. Crediting both would credit a hook that may be entirely inert, which is what the 430 settings hook already was.

intent_constraints: must take effect ONLY on the signed-in user's own profile; the equivalent control on another user's profile must be completely unaffected
a normal tap must still do exactly what it did before
the control must remain visible and usable if the modification cannot attach

supplied_captures.note: The own-profile guard needs two values no anchor line can bind, so they are derived from the matched method instead. profile_action_bar_self_guard proves, in order: ProfileActionBar exists in this version (the SELECTOR - a version without it decides self/other some other way and any value derived here would describe the wrong architecture); instagram_menu_outline_24 re-resolves to a drawable id in THIS version (the NAME is the durable key, the id is not); exactly one register in the enclosing method is tested against 2+ distinct instance-of types (430 tests 11 against p3, 439 tests 10 against p4, and no other register is tested more than once in either); that register is one the anchor bound at this site, so it is live where the payload renders; and exactly one of those subtypes loads the drawable - that is the self-profile type. Derived: p4/LX/0Dxw; on 439 and p3/LX/077N; on 430, which are exactly the values the shipped device-verified builds carry. Every 'exactly one' is checked as uniqueness rather than taken as the first hit, and a candidate that cannot be READ declines rather than being skipped, because skipping it would let 'exactly one matched' be true only because the second was never looked at. The rule was derived from 430 and 439 ONLY and a holdout says how far that reaches: 340 and 300 have no ProfileActionBar, no model-subtype dispatch chain, and no instagram_menu_outline_24 (340 ships instagram_menu_pano_outline_24, a different asset). Both keys fail together below 430 because both are consequences of one rewrite, so 430 and 439 are NOT two independent confirmations - this is a 430+ rule resting on roughly one data point. That is why the agent is the fallback and why the deterministic supplier is written to decline unless every precondition is affirmatively proven; inverting the order would be trusting a one-point rule and escalating only on an obvious error, which is how a version-independent payload once shipped without its guard.

hooks.intent: Open the DFInsta settings dialog by long-pressing Options on the user's own profile (legacy IgActionBar variant)

hosts.note: MEASURED, not proposed by an agent. The host is the one class whose body matches this hook's own five-line anchor: 439 -> LX/0Di2; (1 of 181,421 classes, 26 survived the derived prefilter ':Landroid/view/View$OnLongClickListener;') and 430 -> LX/06X7; (1 of 179,190, 27 survivors), each the host the hand-done port established. Cross-checked against a full unprefiltered match over every class in both decodes: identical result. Note the anchor is doing MORE work here than the by_agent note implies - the same long-click iput appears twice in the host, for Options and for the other-user follow button, and it is the drawable and label lines that separate them; that discrimination is now also what finds the class. WHY THIS IS ENOUGH TO DROP proposer_agreement AND adversarial_verified: the anchor is re-matched against the target decode every port and is the same text the patch is spliced into, so nothing is carried across versions the way a descriptor is. WHAT IS NOT FIXED BY THIS: the adversarial verifier's refutation of the 439 mapping stands untouched - LX/0Di2; is the class this anchor selects on 439, and it may still be the class Instagram never reaches at runtime. Mechanical host discovery answers 'which class', not 'does this run'. The decisive test remains a build carrying only this hook.

constraints: the same long-click iput appears TWICE in the host: once for Options and once for the other-user follow button. The five-line anchor including the drawable and label is what disambiguates.
the marker must be unique to THIS hook: the two settings variants once shared Lcom/dfinstagram/SettingsWrapper; and each read the other's patch as its own
sets the builder's own long-click field rather than attaching to a constructed view

probe.note: Not toggleable, so no two-directional delta exists: the dialog either opens on long-press or it does not. This is the variant that was runtime-inert on 430 while passing every static assertion, so the dialog actually opening is the whole proof. Measured on 439: the dialog opens. NOT individually attributable - the other settings variant declares the same signal on the same surface, and Instagram picks between the two action-bar implementations at runtime, so exactly one is live and the observation cannot say which. Crediting both would credit a hook that may be entirely inert, which is what the 430 settings hook already was.

intent_constraints: must take effect ONLY on the signed-in user's own profile; the equivalent control on another user's profile must be completely unaffected
a normal tap must still do exactly what it did before
the same screen carries other controls that respond to a long press; none of their behaviour may change
